meaning: Usually, when you look at the typical amount or number.
japanese: 平均して。
cue: Someone asks how much sleep you get.
reply: On average, I sleep about six hours a night.
replyJapanese: 平均すると、一晩に6時間くらい寝ています。
transferCue: Report how long callers wait on a helpline.
transferReply: Callers wait four minutes on average before someone answers.
transferReplyJapanese: 電話をかけた人は、応答まで平均4分待ちます。
nuance: No article before average. It goes at the start or end of a clause, usually next to a number.
nuanceJapanese: average に冠詞は付けない。節の最初か最後に置き、たいてい数字と一緒に使う。

meaning: On a ship, plane or train.
japanese: 船や飛行機、列車に乗って。
cue: A flight attendant announces that the plane is ready.
reply: Everyone is on board, so we'll be leaving shortly.
replyJapanese: 皆さまご搭乗になりましたので、まもなく出発いたします。
transferCue: Tell a friend what the ferry offers.
transferReply: There's a small café on board if you get hungry.
transferReplyJapanese: お腹がすいたら、船内に小さなカフェがあるよ。
frame: Be on board (a ship / a plane)
nuance: No article and no of: on board the ship, not on board of the ship. At work, on board also means agreeing to join a plan.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞も of も付けない。on board the ship と言い、on board of the ship とは言わない。仕事では、計画に賛同して加わるという意味にもなる。

meaning: Put in a place where people can look at it.
japanese: 展示されて。陳列されて。
cue: A museum guide talks about a famous painting.
reply: The painting will be on display until the end of March.
replyJapanese: その絵は3月末まで展示されます。
transferCue: Ask a shop assistant about a jacket you saw in the window.
transferReply: Do you still have the jacket that was on display yesterday?
transferReplyJapanese: 昨日飾ってあったジャケットは、まだありますか。
frame: Be on display / put something on display
nuance: No article before display. Be on display is the state, put something on display is the action, and go on display means start being shown.
nuanceJapanese: display に冠詞は付けない。be on display は状態、put something on display は動作、go on display は展示が始まること。

meaning: Working at a particular time, especially in a job with shifts.
japanese: 勤務中で。当番で。
cue: A visitor asks a hospital who is working tonight.
reply: Two nurses are on duty on this ward tonight.
replyJapanese: 今夜この病棟では、看護師が2人勤務しています。
transferCue: A security guard is offered a glass of wine at a party.
transferReply: Thanks, but I can't drink while I'm on duty.
transferReplyJapanese: ありがとうございます。でも、勤務中は飲めないんです。
nuance: No article. It suits jobs with shifts, such as nurses, police officers and guards; office workers say at work. The opposite is off duty.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けない。看護師、警察官、警備員など交代制の仕事に使い、会社員なら at work と言う。反対は off duty。

meaning: Used after a question word to show great surprise or annoyance.
japanese: いったい。一体全体。
cue: You come home and find the kitchen in a mess.
reply: What on earth happened in here while I was out?
replyJapanese: 私が出かけている間に、ここでいったい何があったの？
transferCue: Your brother turns up two hours late for dinner.
transferReply: Where on earth have you been? We were getting worried.
transferReplyJapanese: いったいどこに行ってたの？心配し始めてたんだよ。
frame: What / where / how / why on earth …?
nuance: It comes straight after the question word, with no article. It shows strong surprise or annoyance, so avoid it in polite questions.
nuanceJapanese: 疑問詞の直後に置き、冠詞は付けない。強い驚きやいらだちを表すので、丁寧に尋ねる場面では避ける。

meaning: Burning when it should not be.
japanese: 燃えていて。火がついて。
cue: You see smoke pouring from a parked car.
reply: Call the fire brigade! That car is on fire!
replyJapanese: 消防を呼んで。あの車が燃えてる！
transferCue: Explain how an accident in the kitchen began.
transferReply: The tea towel was on fire before I noticed the smell.
transferReplyJapanese: においに気づいたときには、ふきんはもう燃えていました。
frame: Be on fire / set something on fire
nuance: On fire describes the state. For the moment burning starts, say catch fire, without on. Informally it also praises someone who is doing very well.
nuanceJapanese: on fire は燃えている状態を表す。燃え始める瞬間は on を付けずに catch fire と言う。くだけた言い方では、絶好調の人をほめる意味にもなる。

meaning: At the planned time, not early or late.
japanese: 予定どおりに。
cue: A customer asks how the building work is going.
reply: Don't worry, your new kitchen is still on schedule.
replyJapanese: ご安心ください。新しいキッチンは今も予定どおり進んでいます。
transferCue: A station announcement on a snowy morning.
transferReply: Despite the snow, most trains are running on schedule.
transferReplyJapanese: 雪にもかかわらず、ほとんどの列車は定刻どおり運行しています。
nuance: No article. Ahead of schedule means early and behind schedule means late, so the preposition changes each time.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けない。予定より早いときは ahead of schedule、遅れているときは behind schedule で、前置詞が変わる。

meaning: In addition to something, especially something unpleasant.
japanese: 〜に加えて。〜のうえに。
cue: Explain why your week has been so hard.
reply: I caught a cold on top of all the extra work.
replyJapanese: 仕事が増えたうえに、風邪までひいてしまいました。
transferCue: Complain about the cost of a cheap flight.
transferReply: They charge forty pounds for a suitcase on top of the fare.
transferReplyJapanese: 運賃に加えて、スーツケース1個に40ポンドも取られます。
nuance: Followed by a noun or an -ing form. It usually adds one bad thing to another; on top of that links back to the previous sentence.
nuanceJapanese: あとに名詞か -ing 形が続く。悪いことがさらに重なるときによく使う。on top of that は前の文を受けて「そのうえ」という意味。

meaning: Many in a row, each following the one before.
japanese: 次々に。相次いで。
cue: Describe the street outside a hotel before a wedding.
reply: The taxis pulled up one after another outside the hotel.
replyJapanese: ホテルの前に、タクシーが次々と止まりました。
transferCue: Describe a tiring morning at the office.
transferReply: I had three meetings one after another without a break.
transferReplyJapanese: 休憩なしで、会議が3つ立て続けにありました。
nuance: It follows the verb or the noun it describes. One after the other means the same, and a noun can go in the middle: one problem after another.
nuanceJapanese: 動詞か、説明する名詞のあとに置く。one after the other も同じ意味。one problem after another のように、名詞を間に入れる形もある。

meaning: Because you simply want to know something.
japanese: 好奇心から。ちょっと知りたくて。
cue: Ask a friend a slightly personal question about their new flat.
reply: Out of curiosity, how much rent do you pay here?
replyJapanese: ちょっと気になったんだけど、ここの家賃はいくら？
transferCue: Explain why you went to a talk on a subject you do not study.
transferReply: I only went to the lecture out of curiosity.
transferReplyJapanese: その講義には、ただ好奇心から行ってみただけです。
nuance: No article. At the start of a question it softens something slightly personal, and just out of curiosity is softer still.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けない。質問の前に置くと、少し立ち入った内容をやわらげる。just out of curiosity とすると、さらにやわらかい。

meaning: No longer popular or in style.
japanese: 流行遅れで。すたれて。
cue: Explain why you no longer wear a pair of jeans.
reply: These jeans went out of fashion about ten years ago.
replyJapanese: このジーンズは、10年ほど前に流行遅れになりました。
transferCue: Give your opinion on a classic piece of clothing.
transferReply: A plain white shirt is never out of fashion.
transferReplyJapanese: 無地の白いシャツは、決して流行遅れになりません。
nuance: No article. Go out of fashion is the change and be out of fashion is the state. The opposite is in fashion.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けない。go out of fashion は変化、be out of fashion は状態。反対は in fashion。

meaning: Very suddenly and unexpectedly.
japanese: 突然。どこからともなく。
cue: Describe a near accident on your bike.
reply: A dog appeared out of nowhere and I nearly fell off.
replyJapanese: 犬が突然現れて、もう少しで転ぶところでした。
transferCue: Describe a surprising message from an old classmate.
transferReply: Out of nowhere, she emailed me after fifteen years.
transferReplyJapanese: 15年ぶりに、彼女から突然メールが来ました。
nuance: Common after come and appear, or at the start of a sentence. From nowhere means the same. For surprising news, out of the blue is close.
nuanceJapanese: come や appear のあと、または文頭でよく使う。from nowhere も同じ意味。意外な知らせには out of the blue も近い。

meaning: Not possible to get or achieve.
japanese: 手が届かない。実現できない。
cue: Explain why a young couple are still renting.
reply: A house in the city is out of reach for us.
replyJapanese: 市内の一戸建ては、私たちには手が届きません。
transferCue: Describe a football team after a bad result.
transferReply: After that defeat, the title was out of reach.
transferReplyJapanese: あの敗戦で、優勝には手が届かなくなりました。
frame: Be out of reach for someone
nuance: No article. For names the person, or a possessive goes in the middle: out of our reach. It also describes things you physically cannot touch.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けない。誰にとってかは for で示すか、out of our reach のように所有格を間に入れる。物理的に手が届かないものにも使う。

meaning: Not fit enough for hard exercise.
japanese: 運動不足で、体がなまっている。
cue: You are breathing hard after climbing some stairs.
reply: I'm so out of shape that the stairs tire me out.
replyJapanese: 体がなまりすぎて、階段だけで疲れてしまいます。
transferCue: Describe a friend who gave up sport.
transferReply: He got out of shape after he stopped playing football.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼はサッカーをやめてから、体がなまってしまいました。
nuance: No article. It is about fitness, not body size. The opposite is in shape, and British speakers also say unfit.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けない。体型ではなく、体力についての表現。反対は in shape。イギリスでは unfit とも言う。

phrase: out of sight out of mind
meaning: Used to say that people soon forget what they cannot see.
japanese: 目に入らなくなると、忘れてしまうものだ。去る者は日々に疎し。
cue: Explain where you keep your phone while you study.
reply: I leave my phone in the kitchen. Out of sight out of mind.
replyJapanese: スマホは台所に置いておきます。見えなければ気になりませんから。
transferCue: A friend moved abroad and stopped keeping in touch.
transferReply: He never calls now, so I suppose it's out of sight out of mind.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼はもう電話もくれません。去る者は日々に疎し、ということでしょう。
frame: Out of sight out of mind
nuance: Normally written with a comma after sight. It is said as a complete remark, about people who lose touch or problems you stop thinking about.
nuanceJapanese: ふつうは sight のあとにコンマを入れて書く。それだけで一つの発言として使い、疎遠になった人や、考えなくなった問題について言う。

meaning: Singing or playing notes that are not quite right.
japanese: 音程が外れて。調子が狂って。
cue: Explain why you never go to karaoke.
reply: I always sing out of tune, so I avoid karaoke.
replyJapanese: いつも音程を外すので、カラオケは避けています。
transferCue: Describe the old piano at your grandmother's house.
transferReply: Grandma's piano is badly out of tune, but she still plays.
transferReplyJapanese: おばあちゃんのピアノはひどく音が狂っているけれど、今でも弾いています。
frame: Be / sing / play out of tune
nuance: No article. People sing or play out of tune; an instrument is out of tune. The opposite is in tune.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けない。人は sing / play out of tune、楽器は be out of tune と言う。反対は in tune。

meaning: Say something nice about someone.
japanese: 人をほめる。ほめ言葉を言う。
cue: Tell a friend about a nice moment at work.
reply: My manager paid me a compliment on my presentation today.
replyJapanese: 今日、上司が私のプレゼンをほめてくれました。
transferCue: Explain why your grandfather smiled all through dinner.
transferReply: The waiter paid him a compliment on his Italian.
transferReplyJapanese: ウェイターが、祖父のイタリア語をほめてくれたんです。
frame: Pay someone a compliment on something
nuance: The usual verb is pay; say a compliment is wrong. On introduces the thing you admire. Do not confuse the spelling with complement.
nuanceJapanese: 動詞はふつう pay を使い、say a compliment とは言わない。ほめる対象は on で示す。つづりを complement と混同しないこと。

meaning: A fairly large number of people or things.
japanese: かなり多くの。
cue: Someone asks whether you know anyone at the party.
reply: I know quite a few people here from my old job.
replyJapanese: 前の職場の知り合いが、ここにはかなりいます。
transferCue: Give feedback on a colleague's report.
transferReply: There were quite a few spelling mistakes on the first page.
transferReplyJapanese: 1ページ目には、つづりの間違いがかなりありました。
nuance: It means many, not few. Use it with plural countable nouns; for uncountable nouns say quite a bit of.
nuanceJapanese: 「少ない」ではなく「かなり多い」という意味。数えられる名詞の複数形に使い、数えられない名詞には quite a bit of を使う。

meaning: Used to say that you agree or feel the same.
japanese: 私も同じです。こちらも同感です。
cue: A friend says she is exhausted after the trip.
reply: Same here. I could sleep for a whole day.
replyJapanese: 私も。丸一日眠れそう。
transferCue: A colleague says he hasn't had lunch yet.
transferReply: Same here, actually. Shall we get a sandwich together?
transferReplyJapanese: 実は私もです。一緒にサンドイッチでも買いに行きませんか。
nuance: Informal and spoken. It works after both positive and negative statements, so it replaces both me too and me neither.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた話し言葉。肯定文にも否定文にも返せるので、me too と me neither のどちらの代わりにもなる。

meaning: Used to ask if someone understands your explanation.
japanese: 言っていること、わかりますか。
cue: You are explaining why a poster needs fewer words.
reply: With less text, the poster looks cleaner. See what I mean?
replyJapanese: 文字を減らすと、ポスターがすっきり見えます。言いたいこと、わかりますか。
transferCue: Check that a friend follows your directions on a map.
transferReply: Do you see what I mean about the second turning?
transferReplyJapanese: 2つ目の曲がり角のこと、言っている意味わかる？
aliases: do you see what I mean
nuance: See means understand here. In speech the short form without do you is normal. A listener answers I see what you mean.
nuanceJapanese: この see は「理解する」という意味。会話では do you を省いた形がふつう。聞き手は I see what you mean と答える。

meaning: Used to say you can only believe something surprising when you see it.
japanese: 百聞は一見にしかず。
cue: A friend doesn't believe how big the fish at the market are.
reply: Come to the market with me. Seeing is believing.
replyJapanese: 一緒に市場へ来てみて。百聞は一見にしかずだよ。
transferCue: You visit a famous waterfall after seeing photos of it.
transferReply: I thought the photos were edited, but seeing is believing.
transferReplyJapanese: 写真は加工されていると思っていましたが、百聞は一見にしかずですね。
nuance: A fixed saying, so keep the -ing forms and the present tense. Say it when you doubt a claim, or when your own eyes have just proved you wrong.
nuanceJapanese: 決まった言い回しなので、-ing 形と現在形のまま使う。話を疑っているときや、自分の目で見て考えが変わったときに言う。

meaning: Time when you are not working or busy.
japanese: 空いた時間。余暇。
cue: An interviewer asks about your hobbies.
reply: In my spare time, I repair old bicycles.
replyJapanese: 空いた時間には、古い自転車を修理しています。
transferCue: Explain why you have stopped reading novels.
transferReply: I have so little spare time since the baby arrived.
transferReplyJapanese: 赤ちゃんが生まれてから、自由な時間がほとんどありません。
nuance: The preposition is in, with a possessive: in my spare time, not on or at. Free time means the same and is more common in American English.
nuanceJapanese: 前置詞は in で、所有格を付ける。in my spare time と言い、on や at は使わない。free time も同じ意味で、アメリカ英語ではこちらが多い。

meaning: Do something even though it might fail.
japanese: 思い切ってやってみる。いちかばちか賭ける。
cue: You arrive at a busy restaurant without a booking.
reply: We hadn't booked a table, so we took a chance.
replyJapanese: 予約していなかったので、いちかばちか来てみました。
transferCue: Explain how you got your first job with no experience.
transferReply: The owner took a chance on me, and I'm still grateful.
transferReplyJapanese: 店主が私に賭けてくれたんです。今でも感謝しています。
frame: Take a chance on someone / something
nuance: On introduces the person or thing you decide to trust. It sounds more hopeful than take a risk, which stresses the danger.
nuanceJapanese: on のあとに、賭けてみる相手や物を置く。危険を強調する take a risk より、うまくいくことを期待する響きがある。

meaning: Understand what someone wants without being told directly.
japanese: 遠回しに言われたことを、察する。
cue: A guest stays late although you are clearly tired.
reply: I kept looking at my watch, but he couldn't take a hint.
replyJapanese: 何度も時計を見たのに、彼は察してくれませんでした。
transferCue: A colleague asked about your pay until you changed the subject.
transferReply: She finally took the hint and stopped asking about my salary.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女はやっと察して、私の給料について聞くのをやめました。
frame: Take a hint / take the hint
nuance: Can't take a hint describes someone who never notices. Take the hint is about one particular hint. The speaker drops a hint.
nuanceJapanese: can't take a hint は、いつも察しが悪い人について言う。ある特定のほのめかしには take the hint を使う。ほのめかす側は drop a hint。

meaning: Do something that might be dangerous or go wrong.
japanese: 危険を冒す。リスクを取る。
cue: Explain why you left a safe office job.
reply: I decided to take a risk and open my own café.
replyJapanese: 思い切ってリスクを取り、自分のカフェを開くことにしました。
transferCue: Warn a friend who wants to drive home in bad weather.
transferReply: You're taking a risk if you drive in this snow.
transferReplyJapanese: この雪の中を運転するのは、危険を冒すことになるよ。
nuance: The verb is take, not do or make. The plural take risks describes a general habit. Run the risk of doing something names one particular danger.
nuanceJapanese: 動詞は take で、do や make は使わない。複数形の take risks は、ふだんからの傾向を表す。run the risk of doing something は、特定の危険を挙げる言い方。

meaning: Do something to deal with a problem.
japanese: 行動を起こす。対策を取る。
cue: Parents complain about fast cars near a school.
reply: The council must take action before a child gets hurt.
replyJapanese: 子どもがけがをする前に、議会は対策を取るべきです。
transferCue: Describe how a manager dealt with late deliveries.
transferReply: She took action as soon as customers began complaining.
transferReplyJapanese: お客様から苦情が出始めるとすぐに、彼女は対応に動きました。
nuance: No article: take action, not take an action. It is slightly formal, common in news and at work. On or against names the problem.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けない。take an action とは言わない。やや改まった表現で、ニュースや仕事でよく使う。問題は on や against で示す。

meaning: Take control of something and become responsible for it.
japanese: 責任を持って、指揮を執る。
cue: The team leader is off sick during a busy week.
reply: Can you take charge of the team until Maria returns?
replyJapanese: マリアさんが戻るまで、チームをまとめてもらえますか。
transferCue: Describe what your sister did when the family got lost.
transferReply: My sister took charge and found us a taxi.
transferReplyJapanese: 姉が仕切って、タクシーを見つけてくれました。
nuance: No article before charge, and of names what you control. Take charge is the moment you step in; be in charge is the continuing state.
nuanceJapanese: charge に冠詞は付けず、任されるものは of で示す。take charge は引き受ける瞬間、be in charge は続いている状態。

meaning: Start to produce the result that is wanted.
japanese: 効き目が現れる。効果が出る。
cue: A patient asks a pharmacist about a painkiller.
reply: The tablets should take effect within half an hour.
replyJapanese: この錠剤は、30分以内に効いてくるはずです。
transferCue: Describe the results of a new traffic plan.
transferReply: The changes took effect slowly, but the roads are quieter now.
transferReplyJapanese: 変更の効果はゆっくり現れましたが、今は道路が静かになりました。
nuance: No article and no object. Effect with an e is the noun; affect is the verb. For laws and rules it also means start to apply.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞も目的語も付けない。e で始まる effect は名詞で、affect は動詞。法律や規則については「施行される」という意味にもなる。

meaning: Feel upset because you think a remark is about you.
japanese: 個人への攻撃と受け取って、気を悪くする。
cue: An editor has changed a lot of a new colleague's article.
reply: Don't take it personally. She edits everyone's work heavily.
replyJapanese: 気にしないでください。彼女は誰の原稿にもたくさん手を入れるんです。
transferCue: Describe a friend's reaction to a joke about his cooking.
transferReply: I was only joking, but he took it personally.
transferReplyJapanese: 冗談のつもりだったのに、彼は自分への悪口だと受け取ってしまった。
nuance: Mostly used in the negative to comfort someone: don't take it personally. A noun can replace it: take criticism personally.
nuanceJapanese: 相手を慰める否定形 don't take it personally で使うことが多い。it の代わりに名詞も置ける。例: take criticism personally。

meaning: Give your attention to something.
japanese: 注意を払う。気に留める。
cue: Explain why a company finally changed its packaging.
reply: The company only took notice when customers stopped buying.
replyJapanese: お客が買わなくなって初めて、会社は注意を向けました。
transferCue: Complain that your requests at work are ignored.
transferReply: I've asked twice, but nobody takes notice of my emails.
transferReplyJapanese: 2回お願いしたのに、誰も私のメールを気に留めません。
nuance: No article, and of introduces the thing. The negatives take no notice and not take any notice mean ignore and are very common in British English.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けず、対象は of で示す。否定の take no notice や not take any notice は「無視する」という意味で、イギリス英語でよく使う。

meaning: Feel upset because you think someone has been rude to you.
japanese: 気を悪くする。腹を立てる。
cue: You have to refuse a neighbour's invitation.
reply: I hope she won't take offence if I say no.
replyJapanese: 断っても、彼女が気を悪くしないといいのですが。
transferCue: Describe a guest's reaction to a comment about how he speaks.
transferReply: He took offence at a harmless remark about his accent.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は、なまりについての悪気のない一言に腹を立てました。
nuance: No article, and at introduces the cause. The American spelling is offense. No offence is said before a remark that might upset someone.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けず、原因は at で示す。アメリカ英語のつづりは offense。no offence は、相手が気を悪くしそうなことを言う前に添える。

meaning: Feel pleased and satisfied about something you do or are part of.
japanese: 〜に誇りを持つ。
cue: Praise a baker who checks everything he sells.
reply: He takes pride in every loaf that leaves his bakery.
replyJapanese: 彼は、店から出すパンの一つひとつに誇りを持っています。
transferCue: Describe a village that looks after its streets.
transferReply: People here take pride in keeping the streets clean.
transferReplyJapanese: ここの人たちは、通りをきれいに保つことを誇りにしています。
frame: Take pride in something / in doing something
nuance: The preposition is in, followed by a noun or an -ing form. It suggests you do something carefully because it matters to you, not that you boast.
nuanceJapanese: 前置詞は in で、あとに名詞か -ing 形が続く。自慢するのではなく、大切に思って丁寧に取り組むという含みがある。

meaning: Say or accept that something bad is your fault.
japanese: 責任を負う。罪をかぶる。
cue: A manager speaks after her team misses a deadline.
reply: I'll take the blame, since I approved the plan.
replyJapanese: 計画を承認したのは私ですから、責任は私が負います。
transferCue: Describe a boy who protected his little sister.
transferReply: He took the blame for the broken window to protect her.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は妹をかばって、窓を割った罪をかぶりました。
nuance: Always the blame, and for introduces the problem. It can mean admitting a fault that is yours or covering for someone else.
nuanceJapanese: 必ず the blame の形で、何についてかは for で示す。自分の落ち度を認める場合にも、他人をかばう場合にも使う。

meaning: Move ahead of the others or go first.
japanese: 先頭に立つ。先に立って進む。
cue: Describe an exciting moment in a marathon.
reply: A young runner took the lead in the last kilometre.
replyJapanese: 最後の1キロで、若いランナーが先頭に立ちました。
transferCue: Ask a friend who knows the mountain path to go first.
transferReply: You know the path, so you take the lead.
transferReplyJapanese: 道を知っているんだから、君が先頭を歩いてよ。
nuance: Always the lead. In a race or match it means move into first place; in a group it means go first so that others follow.
nuanceJapanese: 必ず the lead の形。レースや試合では首位に立つこと、集団では先に立って他の人を導くことを表す。

meaning: Make a special effort to do something.
japanese: わざわざ〜する。手間を惜しまない。
cue: Thank a neighbour who brought back your lost cat.
reply: Thank you for taking the trouble to bring her home.
replyJapanese: わざわざ連れて帰ってくださって、ありがとうございます。
transferCue: Complain about a careless report.
transferReply: Nobody took the trouble to check the figures.
transferReplyJapanese: 誰も、数字を確認する手間をかけませんでした。
frame: Take the trouble to do something
nuance: Followed by to and a verb. It praises effort that was not required, so it is common in thanks; in the negative it criticises carelessness.
nuanceJapanese: あとに to と動詞が続く。しなくてもよい手間をかけたことをほめる言い方で、お礼によく使う。否定形では、手を抜いたことへの非難になる。

meaning: Be so beautiful or surprising that you are amazed.
japanese: 息をのむほど美しい。はっとさせる。
cue: Describe reaching the top of a mountain at sunrise.
reply: The view from the top took my breath away.
replyJapanese: 頂上からの眺めに、息をのみました。
transferCue: Describe a bride walking into the decorated hall.
transferReply: The flowers in the hall took her breath away.
transferReplyJapanese: 会場の花を見て、彼女は息をのみました。
nuance: The subject is the thing you see or hear, not the person. The possessive changes: my, her, our. The adjective is breathtaking.
nuanceJapanese: 主語は人ではなく、見たり聞いたりしたもの。所有格は my、her、our のように変わる。形容詞は breathtaking。

meaning: Help you stop thinking or worrying about a problem.
japanese: 悩みや心配事から、気をそらしてくれる。
cue: A friend is nervous while waiting for exam results.
reply: Let's watch a film to take your mind off the results.
replyJapanese: 結果のことを忘れられるように、映画でも見ようよ。
transferCue: Explain why you go running after a hard day.
transferReply: Running always takes my mind off problems at work.
transferReplyJapanese: 走ると、いつも仕事の悩みを忘れられます。
nuance: The subject is the activity that helps. Off is followed by the worry, or simply by it or things: the walk took my mind off things.
nuanceJapanese: 主語は、気を紛らわせてくれる活動。off のあとには悩みの内容か、単に it や things を置く。例: the walk took my mind off things。

meaning: Notice how two things or people are not the same.
japanese: 違いがわかる。見分ける。
cue: Someone asks you to compare a cheap and an expensive coffee.
reply: Honestly, I can't tell the difference between the two coffees.
replyJapanese: 正直なところ、この2つのコーヒーの違いがわかりません。
transferCue: Talk about identical twins in your class.
transferReply: The twins dress the same, so nobody can tell the difference.
transferReplyJapanese: その双子は同じ服を着るので、誰にも見分けがつきません。
frame: Tell the difference between A and B
nuance: Tell means recognise here, so it usually follows can or can't. Between links the two things: tell the difference between butter and margarine.
nuanceJapanese: この tell は「見分ける」という意味で、たいてい can や can't と一緒に使う。2つのものは between でつなぐ。例: tell the difference between butter and margarine。

meaning: Because of someone or something.
japanese: 〜のおかげで。〜のせいで。
cue: Explain how you passed your driving test.
reply: Thanks to my uncle's lessons, I passed first time.
replyJapanese: おじが教えてくれたおかげで、一発で合格しました。
transferCue: Explain why you arrived at the cinema late.
transferReply: We missed the start of the film thanks to the traffic.
transferReplyJapanese: 渋滞のせいで、映画の冒頭を見逃しました。
nuance: Followed by a noun, not a clause. It is usually for good results, but it can blame someone with irony: thanks to you, we're late.
nuanceJapanese: あとには節ではなく名詞が続く。ふつうは良い結果に使うが、皮肉を込めて人を責めることもある。例: thanks to you, we're late。

meaning: Used to accept that bad or unlucky things sometimes happen.
japanese: 人生とはそういうものだ。仕方がない。
cue: You were not chosen for a job you wanted.
reply: I didn't get the job, but that's life.
replyJapanese: その仕事には受かりませんでしたが、まあ、そういうものです。
transferCue: It rains on the day of your picnic.
transferReply: That's life. We'll have the picnic indoors instead.
transferReplyJapanese: 仕方ないね。代わりに家の中でピクニックをしよう。
nuance: Said about small or ordinary disappointments, usually your own. About someone else's serious loss it sounds cold.
nuanceJapanese: ちょっとした失望や、よくある不運について、たいてい自分のことに使う。他人の深刻な不幸に言うと、冷たく聞こえる。

meaning: Used to say an event is more fun with more people.
japanese: 人数は多いほど楽しい。
cue: A friend asks if she can bring her cousin to your barbecue.
reply: Of course she can come. The more the merrier.
replyJapanese: もちろん来ていいよ。多いほうが楽しいから。
transferCue: Invite a new colleague to the office quiz night.
transferReply: Bring your whole team to the quiz. The more the merrier!
transferReplyJapanese: クイズ大会にはチーム全員で来てください。多いほど楽しいですから。
nuance: A fixed reply when someone asks whether extra people may come. It has no verb, so do not add is or are.
nuanceJapanese: もう少し人を呼んでもいいかと聞かれたときの決まった返事。動詞のない形なので、is や are は加えない。

meaning: Used to talk about the present compared with the past.
japanese: 最近は。近ごろは。
cue: Compare how people pay now with ten years ago.
reply: Hardly anyone carries cash these days.
replyJapanese: 最近は、現金を持ち歩く人はほとんどいません。
transferCue: Ask an old friend about his job.
transferReply: What are you doing for work these days?
transferReplyJapanese: 最近はどんな仕事をしているの？
nuance: Used with present tenses, not the present perfect: I walk a lot these days. No preposition: not in these days.
nuanceJapanese: 現在完了ではなく、現在形や現在進行形と使う。例: I walk a lot these days。前置詞は付けず、in these days とは言わない。

meaning: A period when you do not have to work.
japanese: 仕事の休み。休暇。
cue: Ask your manager for a few days away in summer.
reply: Could I take some time off in the second week of August?
replyJapanese: 8月の第2週に、お休みをいただけますか。
transferCue: Explain why a colleague is not answering emails.
transferReply: He's having time off to look after his father.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は父親の世話をするために、休みを取っています。
nuance: Uncountable: some time off, not a time off. Take and have are the usual verbs. It covers holidays, illness and family reasons; a day off is one free day.
nuanceJapanese: 数えられない名詞で、some time off と言い、a time off とは言わない。動詞はふつう take か have。休暇、病気、家庭の事情のどれにも使える。a day off は1日の休み。

meaning: Used to say that the time allowed for something has ended.
japanese: 時間切れです。そこまで。
cue: A teacher ends a written test.
reply: Time's up. Please put your pens down now.
replyJapanese: 時間です。ペンを置いてください。
transferCue: Tell your brother his turn on the computer is over.
transferReply: Your time's up on the computer, so it's my turn.
transferReplyJapanese: パソコンの時間は終わり。次は私の番だよ。
nuance: Almost always the short form; time is up sounds formal. It is said by the person in control of a test, game or turn.
nuanceJapanese: ほとんどの場合、短縮形で言う。time is up は改まって聞こえる。テストやゲーム、順番を管理している人が言う表現。

meaning: Used to add a point that makes a judgement more balanced.
japanese: 公平に言えば。
cue: A friend complains that the waiter was slow.
reply: To be fair, he was serving twenty tables alone.
replyJapanese: 公平に言えば、彼は一人で20卓を担当していたんですよ。
transferCue: Comment on a disappointing film.
transferReply: The ending was weak, but to be fair, the acting was excellent.
transferReplyJapanese: 結末は弱かったけれど、公平に言えば、演技は素晴らしかった。
nuance: It adds a point in defence of someone who has just been criticised. To be fair to her names the person. British speakers also put it at the end of a sentence.
nuanceJapanese: 批判された人や物を弁護する一言を加えるときに使う。to be fair to her のように、相手を示せる。イギリス英語では文末に置くこともある。
